title: Readiness Lens: KPI Roadmap & Operational Runway
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-facing launch readiness canvas focused on the next 8 weeks (roadmap runway) and the measurable KPIs we will use to gate lift-off. Meant to be light-weight — mix of checklist + tracker + short contingency playbooks. Use as the single source for the week-of-launch ops brief.

Quick summary: 
- Product: Hosted API - streaming + fallback model variants
- Launch window: target week-of 2026-04-20 (tentative)
- Primary owners: Priya (product-ops), Ethan (SRE), Maya (Console PM), Liam (Eng lead serving-runtime)
- Launch mode: phased canary -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers

Roadmap runway (8-week view):
Week -8 (now): finalize rollout policy + capacity commit, complete smoke tests on staging, begin canary traffic plan
Week -6: infra runbook dry-run, cost burn estimate locked, SLA/credits agreed with sales for enterprise beta
Week -4: perf tuning + kv-cache baseline captured, latency SLOs validated at median/p95, canary automation ready
Week -2: security/compliance checklist complete (audit logs + KMS check), synthetic evals passing, docs & SDK release candidate
Week -1: staging freeze, deploy canary control plane, ops war-room scheduled
Week 0: phased rollout begins, daily KPI digest + midnight on-call triage window for 72h
Post-launch +2w: adoption signals review, quality regressions check, cost delta report

KPI definitions (gating metrics):
1) Request success rate (SLO gate): 99.5% 30d rolling for canary -> 99.9% for full. Failure modes = 5xx, timeouts.
2) Median latency (payload trimmed): target < 120ms for small requests (<=256 tokens); p95 < 350ms.
3) Cost per 1k tokens (unit economics): within +15% of forecast.
4) Token throughput per GPU (ops metric): baseline >= 75% of staged benchmark.
5) Quality regressions: eval set BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-match score delta <= 1.5 points vs baseline.
6) Customer-facing error rate (user-impacting): <0.1%
7) Rollout adoption: canary acceptance -> increase only if SLOs stable for 24h

Gating checklist (preflight pass/fail heuristics):
- Infra: capacity reserve >= 1.4x expected steady state (pass/fail)
- Routing: fallback route validated and exercised in staging (manual run)
- Observability: tracing hooks + token-level cost stream present (no gaps)
- Security: KMS keys rotated and test decrypt logged, audit export smoke OK
- Data: prompt censoring/safety filters on for canary (test vectors >= 200)
- Rollback plan: documented and tested with a no-drift toggle (fail if manual rollback takes > 15m)

Contingency playbooks (short):
A) Surge containment (sudden 3x traffic above forecast):
  - Step 1: Auto-scale buffer triggered -> add reserved burst capacity; ops page alert to SRE
  - Step 2: If latency p95 > 2x target for 10m -> shift non-critical routes to cheaper model variant (quantized)
  - Step 3: If errors spike > 1% for 15m -> throttle new sessions to 25% and notify sales/customer success
Notes: need immediate Slack channel #launch-traffic and presigned escalation with infra on-call.

B) Quality regression rollback (model-level):
  - Condition: eval regression > 1.5 points OR >= 3 customer complaints in 2 hours about hallucination
  - Action: fallback to previous model variant via routing policy -> pause canary increase; trigger PR to revert model rollout
  - Owner: Maya (confirm quality), Liam (execute revert)

C) Cost overrun (> +25% vs forecast for 24h):
  - Quick actions: enable token-level cap for non-paid beta traffic, switch to batching policy with longer tail latency allowed, engage finance for credit lines
  - Longer term: run Optimize suggestions (quantization + grouping) and schedule dedicated follow-up within 72h

Rollout plan (phased):
- Canary (0.5% traffic, 24h): baseline SLOs observed
- Phase A (5%, 48h): observe KPIs, run targeted synthetic prompts
- Phase B (25%, 72h): check adoption metrics and latency under staging-like mix
- Phase C (60%, 7d): extended soak testing under near-production mix
- Full (100%): only if KPIs stable and no open sevs > P2
Rollback triggers: sustained failure-rate >0.5% for 30m, p95 latency >2x target for 60m, quality fail as above.

Operational dashboard needs (weekly cadence):
- Daily digest (email + slack) with: top 5 customer errors, % traffic by route, cost delta, p50/p95 latency, model fallback events
- Runbook quick-links: rollback, re-route, scale-up, emergency throttle (all one-click in console)
- Owner rotation schedule for war-room (12h shifts first 72h)

Open questions / items to resolve (notes to self):
- Who signs the final SLA adjustments for beta customers? (action: Priya to loop in sales legal)
- Need explicit MTTI target for fallback route (aiming for <5m) - confirm with SRE
- Do we enable predictive batching at canary? risk: hidden latency spikes, +ops complexity
- Confirm which enterprise beta customers are in the first 25% cohort (ask CS)

Links & quick refs:
- Preflight confluence draft: https://confluence.redwoodinc/release/preflight-281
- Perf benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/621
- SRE runbook stub: JIRA-PRODOPS-142

Action items (short):
- Priya: consolidate final KPI thresholds and publish to release channel (due: 2026-03-12)
- Ethan: run infra capacity dry-run and attach logs to confluence (due: 2026-03-15)
- Maya: finalize SDK release notes and ensure docs are behind feature flag (due: 2026-03-18)
- Liam: verify canary automation rollback test completes successfully (due: 2026-03-16)

Notes on doc status: working draft — expects engineering perf numbers to shift once bench runs finish. Keep this file as the operational brief for the launch war room; update daily during the two-week run to go-live.

Unresolved / messy bits (honest Drive-style):
- quick experiment notes: tried enabling prefix-cache in staging, saw 8% lower latency but cpu utilization jumped; need followup
- manual checklist still has a few items that depend on platform-engineering team's migration window (TBD)
- some tags/jira refs will change once we consolidate tickets under the launch epic

End of doc.
